problem_summary.summary: Rotate an integer array to the right by a non-negative number of steps, modifying the original array.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: nums and k. Update nums in place; no value is returned.

brute_force.explanation: Normalize the rotation count, place each value into its rotated position in a temporary array, and copy the result back.
brute_force.correctness_idea: An original index i moves to (i + k) modulo n, which is exactly its destination after k right rotations.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — each element is placed and copied once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — the rotated result is stored separately.

optimized.explanation: Reduce k modulo the array length, reverse the whole array, then reverse the first k entries and the remaining suffix.
optimized.correctness_idea: The first reversal moves the original final k values to the front in reversed order and the prefix reversal restores their internal order; reversing the suffix does the same for the other values.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — the three reversals together perform at most a linear number of swaps.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — reversals use a temporary scalar and indices.

steps.action: Swap both pairs; the middle value stays in place.

steps.event: Reverse the first k entries, range [0, 1].
steps.action: Swap 8 and 0 to restore the order of the moved suffix.

steps.condition: Swap endpoints 2 and 4; the center remains.
steps.action: Reverse the remaining values to complete the right rotation.

edge_cases.case: k is zero or a multiple of nums.length
edge_cases.handling: Modulo makes k zero, so the reversals leave the array unchanged.
All reversals are empty or single-element ranges and the value remains unchanged.
Reducing k modulo the length gives the equivalent rotation.
